transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-17
Start: 16:30 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Kumar (Nimbus CTO), Liam O'Connor (Nimbus ML Eng), Sara Velasquez (Nimbus Head Product)

Summary (auto): quick discovery on model selection for multilingual clinical summarization use-case; evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; heavy context (up to 10k tokens per request), Spanish + English support, tool-calling to access EHR retrieval and de-id pipeline; customer concerned about SOC2, KMS, and latency. Next steps and benchmarks agreed.

[00:00:08] Ava (AE): Okay great, um hi everyone thanks for joining, I'm Ava from Redwood, and with me is Daniel, our solutions engineer.
[00:00:15] Daniel (SE): Hi all, excited to dig in. 
[00:00:18] Priya: Hi thanks, Priya here. Quick time check? This is scheduled 30 minutes but we have 45 -- perfect.
[00:00:25] Ava: Yep we've got about 48 minutes, perfect. We'll do intros then go through current stack and requirements, and then talk model choices -- open models vs curated -- and deployment options.
[00:00:37] Liam: Cool. We're evaluating Redwood for two things: clinical note summarization and patient-facing multi-lingual chat. The heavy one is summarization where prompts can be long, like 8k to 12k tokens.
[00:00:51] Daniel: Okay makes sense. When you say 8 to 12k tokens, is that mostly raw EHR notes concatenated or are you chunking?
[00:01:00] Liam: Mostly concatenated sections, we do some pre-processing but we want the model to see context windows that can be long -- sometimes entire encounter history for a patient.
[00:01:08] Sara: Also multilingual -- Spanish primarily, but also Portuguese and a little French. We care about hallucinations in non-English too.
[00:01:16] Priya: Security is big -- SOC 2 Type II, audit logs, SSO (SAML), and we need to be able to use our HSM for keys for the Private option.
[00:01:24] Ava: Great -- those are common asks. Redwood has Hosted for quick start, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and Private for VPC/on-prem with KMS/HSM integrations. We'll share the SOC2 docs after.

[00:01:40] --- Topics: model context length, multilingual quality, tool-calling / retrieval, deployment mode tradeoffs ---

[00:01:52] Daniel: On the model side -- are you leaning open-weight models or are you okay with provider-managed models? Open models give flexibility to pick quantization and context length tradeoffs, but hosted curated models can be simpler. What are your priorities: latency, cost, or deterministic outputs?
[00:02:06] Priya: Deterministic-ish, but we prioritize safety and cost more than micro-latency. If we can get consistent latency under 400ms token generation for streaming that's fine. Cost is significant -- we're price sensitive.
[00:02:17] Liam: And accuracy in Spanish clinical terminology is non negotiable. We've had models that do well in English but invent terms in Spanish.
[00:02:24] Daniel: Understood. For context length we support model variants: 8k, 32k, and some 64k variants depending on model family. For example, Llama-family forks and Mistral newer long-context variants, also some Falcon variants -- though availability depends on hosting and quantization.
[00:02:42] Ava: To add, Redwood's runtime supports KV-cache optimizations and prefix caching so repeated encounter history can be cached to reduce cost/latency. For Dedicated you can tune batching aggressively.

[00:02:58] [00:03:05] Sara: Can we talk about tool-calling? We need the model to call a retrieval tool that hits our internal EHR index and a de-id tool before returning to patient-facing chat. Function-calling style.
[00:03:18] Daniel: Yes, we support tool or function-calling patterns; Redwood has function-like structured outputs and you can route those calls to your microservices. For Private, you can host the router in VPC so the call never leaves your network. In Hosted, you can set up private network peering or use our Dedicated with private endpoints.
[00:03:36] Priya: For Hosted, data residency is a concern -- is there guaranteed region pinning?
[00:03:41] Ava: Hosted supports region selection, but if you need strict residency and your own network controls, Private is the best fit. Dedicated can be isolated within a cloud region with committed capacity.

[00:03:55] [00:04:10] Liam: About multilingual model quality -- do you have benchmarks or published evals for Spanish clinical?
[00:04:16] Daniel: We have some internal evals; I can share a small benchmark we ran comparing Mistral-xx, Llama2 variants, and Falcon-40B-long. Results vary: some Mistral variants are strong in European Spanish, Llama forks with instruction fine-tune are also solid, but you may need domain fine-tuning or in-context retrieval to reduce hallucination. We'll provide the comparison spreadsheet.
[00:04:38] Priya: Fine-tuning is possible? We can't send PHI to a shared fine-tune service.
[00:04:45] Ava: For PHI we recommend Private deployment with customer-managed storage, or use Redwood's embed-and-retrieve approach where only embeddings (optionally encrypted) are stored and fine-tune is done in a Private tenant. We'll outline options.

[00:04:58] [00:05:12] Sara: Latency vs cost tradeoff -- what does Dedicated buy us?
[00:05:18] Daniel: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools; you can pick lower-precision quantized kernels to lower cost, and set autoscaling. It's generally lower per-token cost at steady state and more predictable latency compared to Hosted bursty pools. But it requires committed spend.
[00:05:33] Liam: Do you support 8-bit/4-bit quantization on these long context models? We've seen memory blow-up at 64k.
[00:05:40] Daniel: Yes, we support INT8/4-bit modes for many families; for 64k you need attention kernel support -- some model families have optimized kernels for long attn. We'll recommend model/kernel pairs for 64k use.

[00:05:54] [00:06:10] Priya: Can you run an offline benchmark for us? We'll provide a few anonymized transcripts and Spanish prompts.
[00:06:17] Ava: Absolutely. For the benchmark, what's the target success metric? F1 on entity extraction, and hallucination rate under X?
[00:06:25] Liam: Hallucination under 5% for medication entities, and summary coherence -- we'll send a rubric. Also throughput requirement: 200 concurrent sessions with average 1.2k tokens per second output across the fleet? Rough numbers.
[00:06:38] Daniel: Great. For that scale Dedicated is likely the practical path; Hosted could work initially but cost may ramp. We'll provide throughput estimates for both.

[00:06:52] [00:07:05] Sara: One more on tool-calling -- do you support synchronous tool calls (model waits) vs async event-style? We have a de-id pipeline that's a few hundred ms.
[00:07:15] Daniel: Both: you can have synchronous calls where the model pauses waiting for a tool response, or you can design an orchestrator that does async followed by a continuation prompt. Redwood's streaming supports partial outputs while you wait. We'll show patterns.

[00:07:30] [00:07:45] Priya: On compliance -- do you provide audit logs at token/request level? We need per-request logging for audits.
[00:07:52] Ava: Yes, Redwood Console provides detailed traces and token-level cost breakdowns; in Private you can forward logs to your SIEM. We'll include sample audit logs.

[00:08:05] [00:08:20] Liam: Are there any models you would recommend off the shelf for Spanish clinical text?
[00:08:27] Daniel: Short answer: we recommend testing a few -- a Llama-instruction-tuned variant for its instruction following, a Mistral-large-long for fluency and some Falcon-40B-long variants. If you need medical fidelity, a domain-adapted Llama fork or a privately fine-tuned checkpoint often wins. We'll include our past eval sheet with notes.

[00:08:45] [00:09:00] Priya: If we go Private, what's the typical deployment timeline?
[00:09:05] Ava: For Private in a VPC with our control plane it's typically 6-8 weeks for production-ready, including HSM/KMS integration and compliance checks. On-prem longer. Dedicated can be as quick as 2-4 weeks for reserved capacity. Hosted is immediate.

[00:09:20] [00:09:40] Sara: Cost sensitivity -- can you show us a worked example for per-encounter cost at 8k tokens vs 32k tokens?
[00:09:47] Daniel: We'll prepare a cost model with per-token and per-request latency estimates across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (including infra amortization). We'll send it with the pricing matrix.

[00:10:05] [00:10:25] Priya: Anything about failover/GRACEful degradation? If Dedicated capacity is saturated, do you offer fallbacks?
[00:10:32] Ava: Yes, Redwood supports routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants or Hosted capacity. You can set SLO-based routing. We'll document failover behaviors.

[00:10:47] [00:11:05] Liam: For the benchmark, can we also include multilingual chat flows with function-calling where the model calls 'get_patient_history' and 'deid_service'?
[00:11:12] Daniel: Absolutely. We'll prototype the function-calling pattern and include latency measurements end-to-end.

[00:11:25] [00:11:40] Ava: Quick check -- do you have constraints on bringing models (self-hosted weights) into Redwood Private?
[00:11:46] Priya: We might have internal PEFT checkpoints from prior vendor work; we prefer to host weights ourselves if possible.
[00:11:53] Daniel: That's supported in Private: you can bring your own weights, and the runtime will compile kernels accordingly. We'll need to validate license compatibility for some checkpoints.

[00:12:08] [00:12:30] Sara: Any notes on tokenization differences across models impacting Spanish accent characters and clinical abbreviations?
[00:12:36] Daniel: Yes tokenization can change token counts and cost -- we'll surface tokenization samples. For Spanish, subword splits are usually okay but clinical abbreviations can fragment; in evaluations we try to normalize.

[00:12:55] [00:13:10] Priya: For SSO we'll want SAML and SCIM provisioning for user roles. Does Redwood support RBAC tied to our IdP?
[00:13:16] Ava: Yes, we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC; for Private you can map roles to your IAM. We'll include a sample SAML metadata file.

[00:13:30] [00:13:45] Liam: A short question about streaming -- can we stream partial summaries to our UI while the rest of the doc processes?
[00:13:52] Daniel: Yes, streaming is supported; you can get partial tokens back as they're generated which helps perceived latency. For long contexts we often stream the high-level summary first then append detailed bullets.

[00:14:10] [00:14:30] Sara: Are there any models with built-in chain-of-thought or better explainability we should consider for clinicians?
[00:14:36] Daniel: Some instruction-tuned models surface their chain-of-thought when prompted, but for clinical explainability we usually rely on structured outputs: ask the model for justification bullets and use retrieval evidence to ground them. The platform can attach provenance from the retrieved docs.

[00:14:55] [00:15:10] Priya: Will you share the benchmark harness you use? We want to run it in our environment for reproducibility.
[00:15:18] Ava: Yes we'll send the harness and instructions; for Private we can help run it with your credentials.

[00:15:30] [00:15:50] Liam: One more -- model updates and versioning. We need to pin a model and have controlled rollouts.
[00:15:57] Ava: Redwood has rollout tooling in the Console: canary, A/B, auto fallback, and model pinning. We'll demo in the next session.

[00:16:10] [00:16:30] Daniel: Ok, if you don't mind I'll propose a concrete plan: 1) Redwood sends pricing + comparison sheet; 2) Nimbus shares sample anonymized dataset and success criteria; 3) Redwood runs a benchmark on Hosted vs Dedicated vs selected Private config with 10k-token contexts and Spanish prompts; 4) schedule deep technical session to discuss kernel/model pairs and bring-your-own-weights.
[00:16:55] Priya: That works. Timeline: we'd like results in two weeks.
[00:17:00] Ava: We'll aim for 10 business days.

[00:17:10] [00:17:30] Sara: Any blockers for starting the benchmark? Data access? 
[00:17:35] Liam: We'll need an NDA for the dataset, and prefer to send de-identified samples.
[00:17:41] Ava: Noted. We'll route NDA and share secure upload.

[00:17:50] [00:18:05] Priya: Cost question -- if we hit production, do you offer committed spend discounts for Dedicated?
[00:18:12] Ava: Yes committed capacity pricing for Dedicated, typically monthly or annual commits with lower per-token. We'll include tiers.

[00:18:25] [00:18:45] Daniel: I also want to flag model families with good long-context kernels: some Falcon-40B-long variants and a few Llama-derivatives have optimized attention. Mistral is doing interesting work on efficiency. For 64k windows we need to test memory and attention kernel support.

[00:18:58] [00:19:15] Priya: On encryption -- we want end-to-end encryption at rest and in transit and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) for Private.
[00:19:21] Ava: Supported: KMS/HSM integrations for Private with BYOK; Hosted supports customer-managed keys in some regions. We'll add clear notes.

[00:19:35] [00:19:50] Liam: For the demo/demo data, can Redwood's SE run a short walkthrough of function-calling with Spanish prompt?
[00:19:57] Daniel: Yes, we can demo a Spanish chat calling a de-id function and a retrieval tool. We'll propose times.

[00:20:10] [00:20:30] Sara: Who will be our main point of contact for technical questions?
[00:20:36] Ava: Daniel will be lead SE, and I'm the account owner.

[00:20:45] [00:21:05] -- brief pause, side conversation about scheduling --
[00:21:25] Priya: Ok let's recap then next steps.
[00:21:30] Ava: Recap: we'll send pricing matrix, SOC2/ISO docs, SAML/SCIM examples, and the model comparison spreadsheet; we'll schedule a 60-min deep-dive to run benchmarks with your anonymized test set (10k token contexts, Spanish + English). Redwood will provision trial Dedicated capacity for the benchmark.
[00:21:53] Liam: I'll send the sample prompts and rubric by Friday.
[00:21:58] Ava: Great. We'll also include recommended model/kernel pairings for 32k/64k contexts and a plan for Private BYOW (bring your own weights).

[00:22:10] [00:22:30] Sara: Any concerns about licensing if we bring weights from previous vendors?
[00:22:37] Daniel: We'll need to review licenses -- some weights have restrictions. We'll flag any issues.

[00:22:45] [00:23:00] Priya: Final note -- show us how rollback works if a new model increases hallucination rate.
[00:23:06] Ava: We'll include a rollback playbook and how to tie alerting to evals in Redwood Optimize.

[00:23:20] [00:23:40] -- closing --
[00:23:45] Ava: Thanks everyone, we'll send the materials and follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark deep-dive.
[00:23:53] Priya: Thanks, talk soon.
[00:23:55] Liam: Thanks.
[00:23:58] Sara: Thanks all.
